item.title: Google DeepMind ties up with ICRISAT to develop plant genome atlas
item.description: The open-access catalogue will use AI to help breeders identify promising plant combinations faster, while the partnership will also support genome mapping for other crops ...
item.dc:creator: Aashish Aryan
item.content:encoded: Google DeepMind and Google.org have partnered with Hyderabad-headquartered International Crops Research Institute for the Semi-Arid Tropics (ICRISAT) to launch an open-access global public genetic atlas aimed at identifying the most promising plant combinations, particularly in sorghum, Google India said. “The resulting AI-supported genetic catalogue is aimed at helping breeders and researchers across the world to develop more resilient and productive sorghum varieties faster than traditional methods, which can involve decade-long trial-and-error processes,” the company said in a blog post. Google DeepMind will also support a three-year postdoctoral fellowship at ICRISAT to help develop tools that can map and characterise genomes for other crops and pulses such as chickpea, groundnut and pigeon pea, the company said. “We aim for this collaboration to unlock the global potential of indigenous climate-resilient crops like sorghum, and to empower the agri ecosystem with cutting-edge tools that strengthen global food security and safeguard present and future generations,” Stanford Blade, deputy director general of research and innovation at ICRISAT, said. Separately, Google is expanding access to its Agricultural Understanding Models to enable developers, startups and researchers to build customised solutions for hyperlocal farming challenges and strengthen agricultural resilience, the company said. The move is aimed at widening access to AI tools that can be used to address local agricultural conditions and improve decision-making across the farm ecosystem. Google’s AI Educator Series, first launched in May this year in partnership with five states, is now being expanded to Bihar and Madhya Pradesh. The series will also be made available as a free online resource accessible to users across the country, Google India said. Google.org, Google’s philanthropic arm, will also provide $15 million to The/Nudge to support the growth of micro, small and medium enterprises in India. “This initiative will fund the development of scalable AI tools to expand small enterprises' access to formal credit, market discovery, and compliance,” the company said.

item.title: Bharti Airtel jumps 4%, sees sharpest intraday gain in 3 months; here's why
item.description: At 11:56 AM, Bharti Airtel was up 3.6 per cent at ₹1,863.40, as compared to a 1.65 per cent rise in the BSE Sensex. The stock was the top gainer among the 30-share Sensex and 50-share Nifty index.
item.dc:creator: Deepak Korgaonkar
item.content:encoded: Bharti Airtel share price movement Bharti Airtel's share price moved 3.9 per cent higher to ₹1,869 on the BSE in Thursday’s intraday deals, recording its sharpest intraday rally in the past three months after Jio Platforms announced its initial public offering (IPO). Earlier, on July 9, 2026, the stock price of the telecom services provider surged 3.98 per cent. At 11:56 AM, Bharti Airtel was up 3.6 per cent at ₹1,863.40, as compared to a 1.65 per cent rise in the BSE Sensex. The stock was the top gainer among the 30-share Sensex and 50-share Nifty index. However, thus far in the calendar year 2026, Bharti Airtel has declined 12 per cent in line with the Nifty 50’s fall. The stock hit a 52-week low of ₹1,726.30 on October 1, 2026. It touched a 52-week high of ₹2,174.50 on November 11, 2025. What’s driving Bharti Airtel stock price? Jio Platforms Ltd (JPL), the Reliance Industries (RIL)-controlled digital services company that houses India’s largest telecom operator Reliance Jio, will launch its IPO next week in a price band of ₹1,065-1,119 a share. The IPO is set to become India’s largest, with JPL seeking to raise ₹30,213 crore at the upper end of the price band, valuing it at about ₹10.3 trillion. According to reports, grey market activity indicates strong investor interest in the digital and telecom arm of RIL. According to websites tracking grey market activities, the grey market premium (GMP) surged to around ₹220 on Wednesday evening as soon as the IPO details were announced. This implied a premium of 20 per cent over the upper-end of the price band. On Thursday morning, the premium moderated, but Jio Platforms shares traded at a significant premium in the grey market. Last check, Jio Platforms shares traded at ₹1,319, implying a premium of ₹200 per share, or 17.87 per cent over the upper-end of the price band, the Business Standard reported. READ MORE The key debate going into the JPL IPO is its potential impact on Bharti Airtel, as there could be a shift in telecom sector allocations with another large listed investible option. However, analysts at Motilal Oswal Financial Services (MOFSL) believe concerns around a partial shift in the telecom allocation weight from Bharti Airtel to JPL are overblown, given JPL’s limited initial free float (vs. Bharti’s FII/DII ownership). Further, with expectations of a tariff hike soon after JPL’s IPO, the brokerage firm expects strong earnings delivery, which could also lead to potential multiple re-rating for both Bharti Airtel and JPL. Meanwhile, the delay in implementing a tariff hike (vs. initial expectations of December 2025) has been a key reason for the muted stock performance of Bharti Airtel and RIL vs. Nifty 50, in analysts' view. After the JPL IPO and Vodafone Idea’s impending fundraise, MOFSL believes the case for a tariff hike is stronger and builds in a smartphone tariff hike of 15 per cent in December 2026, which should provide visibility on delivering 15 per cent earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) compound annual growth rate (CAGR) over FY26-29E. Disclaimer: Views and outlook in this report belong to the brokerages and analysts cited. They do not reflect the views of Business Standard. Readers are advised to exercise discretion.

item.title: India may need rate hikes, tax relief to ease pressure on rupee: Analysts
item.description: The rupee's rebound after the RBI's latest measures may prove short-lived as energy import dependence and weak capital inflows weigh on the currency; further rate hikes could help address the pressure ...
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded: By Subhadip Sircar India’s central bank has mounted its strongest defense of the rupee in more than a decade, and said it’s not done yet.The Reserve Bank of India’s measures helped the currency rebound from a near-record low, but analysts are questioning how long the relief can last given India’s heavy dependence on energy imports. The central bank would consider further measures, if needed, to curb speculative trading in the market, Governor Sanjay Malhotra said Tuesday.   Here’s a look at further steps Indian authorities can consider:Bigger Rate HikesThe central bank last week raised interest rates for the first time in nearly four years and signaled further hikes. Unlike some of its Asian peers, the RBI has refrained from using monetary tightening to support the currency, but rising price pressures and a narrowing yield gap with the US are giving it reasons to turn hawkish. The rupee continues to face a capital inflow problem, with a sharp drop in net foreign direct investment causing the currency to be far more dependent on volatile foreign portfolio inflows than in the past, according to MUFG Bank Ltd.  “Higher rates are one way to resolve the fundamental imbalance and is one key reason why we are forecasting RBI to hike rates further,” said Michael Wan, senior currency analyst at the lender.Hiking MSF RateThe RBI can raise its emergency lending rate for banks, making funds more expensive and tightening liquidity to support the rupee. The so-called Marginal Standing Facility currently stands 25 basis points above the key policy rate. The RBI last raised the MSF rate independently of the repo rate to defend the rupee in 2013. During the taper tantrum, the rate was raised by 200 basis points, widening the spread over the policy rate. The measure briefly slowed the rupee’s slide.  “Enhanced corridor on the upper side by increasing MSF rate will result in higher price of the rupee,” said Soumya Kanti Ghosh, chief economic adviser at State Bank of India.Long-term Capital Gains Tax CutA cut in the long-term capital gains on stocks could bring inflows and support the rupee, according to IIFL Capital. Foreigners have been relentless sellers of Indian stocks with net outflows exceeding $30 billion so far this year as investors shifted funds toward markets offering greater exposure to the artificial-intelligence trade. Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman said at the Bloomberg New Economy Forum on Tuesday that “the long-term capital gains tax is something on which a lot of people have been commenting,” but she would “tread cautiously” on the question of taxation very close to the budget. Greater Exchange Rate FlexibilityThe central bank should also look at allowing a more flexible exchange rate, according to Nomura Holdings Inc. and Emkay Global Financial Services. “A durable solution requires greater exchange-rate flexibility, allowing the rupee to adjust gradually rather than through episodic corrections,” said Madhavi Arora, chief economist at Emkay. The central bank has been intervening in the currency market in recent weeks to check rupee volatility. The RBI has repeatedly said that it doesn’t target a specific level for the currency. Lower Exporter Proceed Realisation TimelineAuthorities could further shorten the deadline for exporters to bring their overseas earnings back to India to six months, in line with the typical credit period for export payments, according to a State Bank of India note. The RBI had cut the timeline to nine months in June after extending it to 15 months last year when the US imposed punitive tariffs on India.Raising Fuel PricesRaising domestic fuel prices to reduce fiscal pressure and consumer demand for oil is an option, Nomura economists including Sonal Varma wrote in a note. Such as move can curb fuel demand over time, potentially reducing India’s oil-import bill and demand for dollars, thereby supporting the rupee. India’s state run refiners that command over 90% of the market have kept diesel and gasoline prices unchanged since May 25. Private retailers, however, have raised prices. State refiners are losing ₹530 crore daily on discounted fuel sales, according to Icra Ltd. Lowering LRS LimitsIndividuals in India can send foreign exchange for travel and education among other things under the so-called Liberalized Remittance Scheme. Currently, the annual limit for such transfers is $250,000. Tightening the LRS, as was done in 2013, is an option, according to an Ambit Capital note by analysts Swayamsiddha Panda and Eashaan Nair.

item.description: Speaking at the Raisina Dialogue's Middle East edition in Abu Dhabi, the external affairs minister said countries must explore new partnerships and move beyond traditional comfort zones ...
item.content:encoded:
Home / External Affairs Defence Security / News / Jaishankar calls for urgent multilateral reform amid changing global order

Jaishankar calls for urgent multilateral reform amid changing global order Speaking at the Raisina Dialogue's Middle East edition in Abu Dhabi, the external affairs minister said countries must explore new partnerships and move beyond traditional comfort zones

Jaishankar cited the India-UAE partnership over the past decade as an example of how countries have responded to a changing global environment | Image: Bloomberg

Press Trust of India Abu Dhabi 3 min read Last Updated : Oct 15 2026 | 9:47 AM IST

Listen to This Article

External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar called for "urgent" reform of multilateral institutions to reflect the changing global order, saying stronger cooperation among smaller groups of countries could support the process. Jaishankar made the remarks during a session of the Raisina Dialogue's Middle East edition in Abu Dhabi on Wednesday, where he joined UAE Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Sheikh Abdullah bin Zayed Al-Nahyan for a discussion on 'The World Ahead: Power, Purpose & Possibility'. Highlighting the increasing pace of change in the global order during the conversation, the minister said it reflected both "long-term trends and immediate shocks", prompting countries to explore new partnerships and alternatives in response to their specific circumstances.

"New partnerships and fresh options are inevitably explored in that pursuit," he said in a social media post after the discussion. This required countries to move beyond traditional comfort zones and develop sharper strategic awareness, Jaishankar said. Also Read

LAC must be stable for normalisation of ties with China: EAM Jaishankar

India-US trade deal talks nearing 'landing point', says Jaishankar

Jaishankar outlines key foreign policy objectives on US, China, Russia ties

India rejects China's objection to standard names for 28 Ladakh places

MEA rejects UN rights body's concerns over Delhi protest restrictions

"The reform of multilateralism is urgent. It can be supported through stronger minilateralism," he underlined. Minilateralism refers to cooperation among a relatively small group of countries to address specific issues, often allowing them to work together more effectively when broader multilateral forums struggle to reach consensus. Jaishankar cited the India-UAE partnership over the past decade as an example of how countries have responded to a changing global environment.

"The India-UAE partnership of the last decade is a great example of our two nations responding to the changing global environment," he said. Separately, Jaishankar also held a bilateral meeting with Zayed Al-Nahyan, describing it as "warm and productive". They exchanged views on bilateral and global issues in the spirit of the Comprehensive Strategic Partnership between the two countries. Jaishankar arrived in the UAE on Wednesday for a three-day official visit to review progress in bilateral ties. India and the United Arab Emirates (UAE) have expanded their cooperation across trade, investment, energy, defence and security in recent years. The Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA), which came into force in May 2022, has provided a framework for boosting bilateral trade and economic engagement.

The UAE is also an important partner for India in the Gulf region, home to a large Indian expatriate community and a key source of energy supplies and investment. According to the Embassy of India in Abu Dhabi, the Indian expatriate community is the largest ethnic community in the UAE, accounting for approximately 35 per cent of the country's population. The number of resident Indian nationals in the UAE was estimated at 4.3 million in 2024. Around 15 per cent of the Indian diaspora lives in the Emirate of Abu Dhabi, while the rest is spread across the other six emirates, including Dubai.

Among Indian states, Kerala has the largest representation, followed by Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh and Telangana. People from Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Punjab and other states also constitute significant sections of the Indian community.

(Only the headline and picture of this report may have been reworked by the Business Standard staff; the rest of the content is auto-generated from a syndicated feed.)
